name: Civil unrest
value: France strike day drew 146,000 on 17 Nov
summary: France's 17 Nov strike day drew 146,000 by official count and 500,000 by unions' count; protests stayed largely peaceful
state: A nationwide strike and protest day over pay and living costs in France on 17 Nov drew 146,000 people by the interior ministry's count and 500,000 by unions' count, the latest in weekly protests since October, and unions said they would keep up pressure (Bloomberg; Al Jazeera). No deaths were reported. Sustained protests in several countries keep Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest in a major country was found as of 19 Nov.
for_you: Travellers in France may face transport strikes and road disruption on protest days. FCDO travel advice for France lists current disruption.
rubric_hit: Significant protests in several countries (France 17 Nov: 146,000 by official count); no deadly nationwide unrest (Watch)

sources.title: Bloomberg — Unions rally 146,000 in France over cost of living and wage demands
Al Jazeera — More than 100,000 take part in France pay protests

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
